olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Two players alternate with a pile of 2003 stones. First player picks a divisor of 2003 to remove; subsequent players pick a divisor of the remaining count to remove. The player forced to remove the last stone loses. Find the winning strategy.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Circle $S$ with diameter $AB$; tangent at $B$ meets points $C,D$ with $B$ between them. $E,F$ are intersections of $S$ with $AC,AD$; $G,H$ are intersections of $S$ with $CF,DE$. Show $AH=AG$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $a,b>0$ with $a>1$ and $b>2$. Prove $a^b+1\geq b(a+1)$ and find when equality holds.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Two circles $S_1,S_2$ intersect at $P,Q$. Parallel lines $\ell_1$ through $P$ and $\ell_2$ through $Q$ meet $S_1,S_2$ at $A_1,A_2$ and $B_1,B_2$. Show $\triangle A_1QA_2$ and $\triangle B_1PB_2$ have the same perimeter.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: An $8\times 8$ board: each cell is black or white. Count colorings where every $2\times 2$ square (with 4 squares sharing a vertex) has exactly 2 white and 2 black cells.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Call $n$ \textit{tico} if the digit sum of $n$ is a multiple of 2003. (i) Show there exists $N$ with $N,2N,\ldots,2003N$ all tico. (ii) Does there exist $N$ with all multiples tico?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2003
